profile.description: Departmental AI strategy and adoption statements. Named speakers retain separate profiles.

summary.text: In a 2023 fact sheet, the Department said it had been investing in AI and responsibly fielding data- and AI-enabled systems for over 60 years, and that its 2023 data, analytics, and AI strategy built upon and superseded its 2018 AI and 2020 data strategies. The 2023 materials placed Responsible AI at the top of the Department's AI Hierarchy of Needs, described quality data as the foundation, and said assurance processes for testing, evaluation, validation, and verification are imperative for Responsible AI. A January 2026 release announced an AI Acceleration Strategy intended to extend the Department's lead in military AI deployment, while a December 2025 release said the Department was providing no-cost GenAI.mil training to all DoW employees. The Department's ai.mil page describes providing Department-wide access to frontier generative AI models, such as Google's Gemini and xAI's Grok, for DoW personnel at Impact Level 5 and above.

statements.text: The DoD has been investing in AI and responsibly fielding data- and AI-enabled systems for over 60 years.

attribution.speaker: Department of War / Defense

statements.text: This 2023 DoD Data, Analytics, and AI Adoption Strategy builds upon and supersedes the 2018 AI Strategy and the 2020 Data Strategy to continue the Department’s digital transformation.

attribution.speaker: Department of War / Defense
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The Department will focus strategic efforts on several interdependent goals that support the DoD AI Hierarchy of Needs.

attribution.speaker: Department of War / Defense
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: At the top of the pyramid is Responsible AI, the Department’s dynamic approach to the design, development, and use of AI capabilities that is consistent with the DoD AI Ethical Principles.

attribution.speaker: Department of War / Defense
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The Department will focus strategic efforts on several interdependent goals that support the DoD AI Hierarchy of Needs (Figure 2). The AI Hierarchy of Needs is a pyramid with quality data as its foundation since all analytic and AI capabilities require trusted, high-quality data to support decision makers.

attribution.speaker: Department of War / Defense
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The layers of the Hierarchy are supported by robust sets of processes. Increased data quality and insightful analytics are achievable through effective enterprise data governance. Sound assurance processes for testing, evaluation, validation, and verification are imperative for Responsible AI.

attribution.speaker: Department of War / Defense
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The Hierarchy is helpful as a framework for assessing DoD AI readiness, and for guiding the Department’s goals to accelerate adoption of data, analytics, and AI technologies to build enduring decision advantage.

attribution.speaker: Department of War / Defense
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: We do not develop or deploy AI capabilities unless they are aligned with DoD's AI Ethical Principles.

attribution.speaker: Department of War / Defense
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The Department of War today launches a transformative Artificial Intelligence Acceleration Strategy that will extend our lead in military AI deployment and establish the United States as the world's undisputed AI-enabled fighting force.
